disclosures.name: TestAllThreadsSyscall
disclosures.signature: AllThreadsSyscall disabled with cgo
disclosures.reason: The converted corpus is behaviourally a cgo-LINKED Go build for this package, and the oracle is pinned cgo-OFF; this verdict is the residue of that mismatch, not a capability gap. Measured at the pinned state (go1.23.12 linux/amd64, Release, tiering off): Go=pass, C#=skip. Go passes because at CGO_ENABLED=0 its runtime really does stop the world and replay the syscall on every thread. The converted side skips because runtime_doAllThreadsSyscall answers ENOTSUP -- and that is not a stub evading the question: ENOTSUP is the answer a cgo-linked Go build gives, which is why this very test opens by skipping on it with the message pinned as this entry's signature. Go's own source names the configuration in that string. Since the cgocaller keystone's Linux increment 1, the corpus is unambiguously that configuration in BOTH halves -- the nine credential wrappers route through libc's setxid broadcast (TestSetuidEtc passes, 21 assertions) AND the raw AllThreadsSyscall answers ENOTSUP -- so the two facts are coherent rather than the lone gap they were before. The oracle cannot be moved to match: the corpus's Go FILE SELECTION was emitted at CGO_ENABLED=0, both comparison sides must share one cgo state, and the converted side can only be the corpus's. SCOPE NOTE: at cgo-ON the oracle would itself be cgo-linked and skip here too, so the row would read skip/skip and AGREE -- but that agreement would be a coincidence of errno rather than evidence of fidelity, which is precisely why this is disclosed rather than pinned away by a cgo flag. RETIREMENT: if the managed runtime ever gains a real all-threads broadcast, these three verdicts go pass/pass and this entry retires itself.

disclosures.name: TestPrlimitFileLimit
disclosures.signature: pipe2: too many open files
disclosures.reason: The managed runtime's descriptor floor exceeds 43. The test lowers the process's SOFT RLIMIT_NOFILE to 43 (magicRlimitValue + 1, syscall_linux_test.go:720-734) and then opens two pipes; a Go test binary holds a handful of descriptors, the converted host holds far more -- 163 when GolibTests' LinuxDescriptorLimitTests measured it on the WSL arm (2026-09-23, go1.24.13) -- so the first os.Pipe fails EMFILE here and passes in Go. The CLR's own thread start needs 2 free descriptors under that limit (same arm; a native pthread_create needs none), which is why the test host now restores RLIMIT_NOFILE after each top-level test (testing/HostDescriptorLimit.cs): before that, this one verdict took the rest of the syscall row down with it, OutOfMemoryException out of Thread.StartCore at the next test's start and 19 rows never run. Measured, not argued: the row re-read with the restore in place runs 56 of 56.

disclosures.name: TestRlimitRestored
disclosures.signature: rlimit not adjusted at startup
disclosures.reason: The .NET runtime raises the process's RLIMIT_NOFILE soft limit to its hard limit while it initializes, before any managed code runs (P2 measured it on .NET 10.0.12: a probe launched at soft 1024, 19998 and 20000 read 20000/20000 every time). Go's syscall init (rlimit.go) raises the soft limit to Max-1 and saves the original in origRlimitNofile only when it finds Cur < Max-1, and StartProcess restores that original in each child. The converted init (src/core/syscall/linux/rlimit.cs) is faithful -- setrlimit is real and the exec path reads origRlimitNofile -- but it always finds Cur == Max, so it saves nothing, and the test takes the branch Go's own source wrote for exactly that state: `t.Skip("skipping test because rlimit not adjusted at startup")` (exec_unix_test.go:353). Go passes on a host whose soft limit starts below Max-1 and skips with the same line where it does not, so the entry fires only on the first kind of host; elsewhere both sides skip and agree. The class is the verdict shape (Go pass / converted skip), not a defect in the converted code: the original limit is gone before managed code exists, and restoring it needs native code that runs before the runtime initializes (a custom host or a preload constructor; no runtime setting was found). Self-retiring: the entry stops firing the day the host preserves the original soft limit. Rooted by P2 (BOARD, 2026-10-25, "exec children inherit the CLR-raised NOFILE soft limit"); class ruled by COORD 2026-10-25 06:29Z and 06:58Z; authored by G, 2026-10-25. The signature is Go's own skip text, which the converted host prints verbatim.

Self-retiring in this class's required way: the entry stops firing the moment the spawn seam gains Chroot -- no corpus change and no manifest edit. runtime-capability's refusal does not apply: nothing here is unimplemented-but-fixable, and the managed fork-window dance that could express these fields was DELIBERATELY retired for file-descriptor-hygiene soundness, which is a ruled correctness decision rather than an omission.
